answer: Mix hidden calibration items into every grading queue, answers whose fair score is already known, much as a geologist slips a labelled quartz sample into a tray of unknown rocks. Graders who misjudge them lose weight. A sybil swarm that rubber-stamps everything fails together, leaving a plume of identical errors that stands out at once. Weight earned this way accrues at glacier pace, so a fresh batch of keys cannot buy influence overnight.
